```{python}
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat

import itertools as _it

DOC = "PCR-005"
UO = "protein_a"
UO_TITLE = "Protein A Chromatography (Step 5)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (pulled from the model; nothing typed) --------------
ALPHA = 0.05                                   # significance level used throughout

P = CFG.unit_op(UO)
PARAMS = report_params(UO)
n_params = len(PARAMS)
cls_n = PARAMS["Class"].value_counts().to_dict()
n_wccpp = cls_n.get("WC-CPP", 0)
n_kpp = cls_n.get("KPP", 0)
n_gpp = cls_n.get("GPP", 0)
n_cpp = cls_n.get("CPP", 0)
n_mv = int((PARAMS["Study"] == "multivariate").sum())
n_uv = n_params - n_mv

FCT = D.rsm_factors(UO)

LBL = {r: D.RESP_LABEL[r] for r in RESP}

scr = csv(f"doe_{UO}_screening.csv")
rsm = csv(f"doe_{UO}_rsm.csv")
n_scr, n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "screening"), doe_runs(UO, "rsm")

n_scr_fact = int((scr.run_type == "factorial").sum())
n_rsm_fact = int((rsm.run_type == "factorial").sum())
n_rsm_ax = int((rsm.run_type == "axial").sum())
n_scr_terms = len(D.screening_effects_df(UO, HCP))
n_rsm_terms = len(D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, HCP))

fit_s = {r: D.fit(UO, "screening", r) for r in RESP}
fit_r = {r: D.fit(UO, "rsm", r) for r in RESP}
cv_s = D.center_cv_df(UO, "screening").set_index("Response")
cv_r = D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm").set_index("Response")

cp_hcp_sd = float(cv_r.loc[LBL[HCP], "SD"])

acc_hcp = D.acceptance_for(UO, HCP)
acc_lpa = D.acceptance_for(UO, LPA)

# highest leached Protein A actually measured in either reported design
lpa_meas_hi = float(max(rsm[LPA].max(), scr[LPA].max()))

# term-level statements about the pool HCP surface, read off its own coefficient table
CO_HCP = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, HCP)


def hcp_term(term, col="Coef."):
    return float(CO_HCP.loc[CO_HCP["Term"] == term, col].iloc[0])


_is_2fi = (CO_HCP["Term"].str.len() == 2) & (~CO_HCP["Term"].str.contains("²"))
n_sig_2fi = int((_is_2fi & (CO_HCP["p-value"] < ALPHA)).sum())
ad_over_ab = abs(hcp_term("AD")) / abs(hcp_term("AB"))
bd_over_ab = abs(hcp_term("BD")) / abs(hcp_term("AB"))
p_flow_hcp = hcp_term("C", "p-value")


def pred(resp, **coded):
    """Fitted response-surface prediction; unnamed factors sit at their set-points."""
    s = {f: 0.0 for f in FCT}
    s.update(coded)
    return float(D.predict(UO, resp, coded=s)[0])


def _corner(resp, want_max=True):
    rows = [(dict(zip(FCT, c)), pred(resp, **dict(zip(FCT, c))))
            for c in _it.product([-1.0, 1.0], repeat=len(FCT))]
    rows.sort(key=lambda t: t[1], reverse=want_max)
    return rows[0]


def corner_str(c):
    parts = []
    for f, v in c.items():
        p = P.param(f)
        u = "" if p.unit == "pH" else f" {p.unit}"
        parts.append(f"{p.name.lower()} {D.to_natural(UO, f, v):g}{u}")
    return ", ".join(parts[:-1]) + " and " + parts[-1]


hcp_sp, yld_sp, lpa_sp = pred(HCP), pred(YLD), pred(LPA)

# the two edges of the contour plane, read as predictions instead of off the figure
hcp_lo_ph = (pred(HCP, load=-1, elution_ph=-1), pred(HCP, load=1, elution_ph=-1))
hcp_hi_ph = (pred(HCP, load=-1, elution_ph=1), pred(HCP, load=1, elution_ph=1))
load_penalty_ratio = ((hcp_lo_ph[1] - hcp_lo_ph[0]) / (hcp_hi_ph[1] - hcp_hi_ph[0]))

hcp_corner, hcp_hi = _corner(HCP, True)
hcp_lo = _corner(HCP, False)[1]
lpa_corner, lpa_hi = _corner(LPA, True)
yld_corner, yld_lo = _corner(YLD, False)

# the design run executed at the worst-case corner for leached Protein A
_at_corner = rsm.index[np.all([rsm["coded_" + f] == v for f, v in lpa_corner.items()],

lpa_corner_run = int(rsm.loc[_at_corner, "run"])
lpa_corner_obs = float(rsm.loc[_at_corner, LPA])

nor_c = {f: [float(D.to_coded(UO, f, P.param(f).nor[0])),
             float(D.to_coded(UO, f, P.param(f).nor[1]))] for f in FCT}


def nor_extreme(resp, want_max=True):
    vals = [pred(resp, **{f: nor_c[f][i] for f, i in zip(FCT, c)})
            for c in _it.product([0, 1], repeat=len(FCT))]
    return max(vals) if want_max else min(vals)


# extrema over the whole characterized region, not only its corners: the quadratic
# terms mean an interior or face point can beat every corner. ph_hi caps the elution
# buffer pH axis, so the same scan can be run over the capped design space.
def region_extreme(resp, want_max=True, ph_hi=1.0):
    axes = [np.linspace(-1.0, ph_hi if f == "elution_ph" else 1.0, 13) for f in FCT]
    g = np.array(list(_it.product(*axes)))
    y = D.predict(UO, resp, coded={f: g[:, i] for i, f in enumerate(FCT)})
    return float(y.max() if want_max else y.min())


reg_hcp_hi, reg_hcp_lo = region_extreme(HCP, True), region_extreme(HCP, False)
reg_lpa_hi = region_extreme(LPA, True)
reg_yld_lo = region_extreme(YLD, False)
hcp_span_fold = reg_hcp_hi / reg_hcp_lo

nor_hcp_hi, nor_hcp_lo = nor_extreme(HCP, True), nor_extreme(HCP, False)
nor_lpa_hi = nor_extreme(LPA, True)
nor_yld_lo = nor_extreme(YLD, False)

par_lpa_ph_sp = D.par_at_design_centre(UO, LPA, "elution_ph")["par_nat"]
par_lpa_ph_nor = D.par_nor_propagated(UO, LPA, "elution_ph")["par_nat"]

reg_lpa_hi_cap = region_extreme(LPA, True, ph_hi=ph_cap_coded)
gov_hcp = D.governing_factor(UO, HCP)
gov_lpa = D.governing_factor(UO, LPA)

co_hcp = fit_r[HCP]["model"].params
d_over_b = abs(co_hcp["end_collect"]) / abs(co_hcp["elution_ph"])

# capability, method performance, equipment, prior documents, train context
CAPR = cap.set_index("key")
CAPK = ["leached_protein_a", "hcp", "residual_dna"]
hcp_sigma_margin = ((CAPR.loc["hcp", "acc_high"] - CAPR.loc["hcp", "mean"])
                    / CAPR.loc["hcp", "sd"])
hcp_over_limit_sp = hcp_sp / acc_hcp[1]
hcp_over_limit_min = reg_hcp_lo / acc_hcp[1]
MPERF = method_perf_df().set_index("Method")
STEP_AMVS = [a for a, _ in PROTEIN_A_AMV_REFS]
EQ = equipment_df().set_index("Equipment")
PRIOR = csv("dev_prior_docs.csv").set_index("id")
LOTS = csv("dev_lots.csv").set_index("id")
PS = csv("process_summary.csv").set_index("step")

pa_hcp_nom = float(PS.loc[P.step, "pool_hcp_ng_mg"])
pa_lpa_nom = float(PS.loc[P.step, "leached_protein_a_ppm"])
cex_fold = float(PS.loc[CFG.unit_op("cex").step, "hcp_clearance_fold"])

ds_hcp_nom = float(PS.loc[CFG.unit_op("aex").step, "hcp_out_ng_mg"])

# deviation facts (DEV-005-01 / DEV-005-02), all from the seeded register
DEVS = dev_facts(DOC).set_index("dev_id")

dev1_lot = DEVS.loc["DEV-005-01", "lot"]
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Protein A affinity chromatography is the capture step of the A-Mab drug substance process
and the first chromatographic operation in the purification train. It is the step at which
leached Protein A enters the process, and it provides the principal clearance of host cell
protein and residual DNA. This report presents the characterization executed under PCP-005
on a qualified scale-down model, in support of the transfer of the drug substance process to
commercial manufacture. The study follows the lifecycle approach to process validation
[@fda2011] and the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11, with the published
A-Mab case study as the source of the process model [@amab2009].

`{python} f"{n_params}"` parameters were characterized. `{python} f"{n_mv}"` were carried
into a multivariate design and `{python} f"{n_uv}"` were assessed one at a time. The outcome
is `{python} f"{n_wccpp}"` well-controlled critical process parameters,
`{python} f"{n_kpp}"` key process parameters and `{python} f"{n_gpp}"` general process
parameters. No parameter at this step is a critical process parameter, which is consistent
with the platform experience described in @sec-prior.

The multivariate work comprised a screening design of `{python} f"{n_scr}"` runs and a
face-centred central composite design of `{python} f"{n_rsm}"` runs in protein load, elution
buffer pH, load flow rate and end of pool collect. The screening design identified which
factors are active. The response-surface model is the predictive model and the basis of the
design space. Pool HCP is described by a strong surface (R² =
`{python} f"{fit_r[HCP]['R2']:.3f}"`, predicted R² =
`{python} f"{fit_r[HCP]['predR2']:.3f}"`), on which elution buffer pH carries the largest
main effect. The step yield model is adequate. No factor effect on leached Protein A was
resolved, and no predictive claim is made for that response.

Leached Protein A is the one CQA this step sets. The highest value measured anywhere in the
two designs was `{python} f"{lpa_meas_hi:.2f}"` ppm, against an acceptance criterion of
`{python} f"{acc_lpa[0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{acc_lpa[1]:g}"` ppm, and the fitted model gives
`{python} f"{lpa_sp:.2f}"` ppm at the set-point and a mean of no more than
`{python} f"{reg_lpa_hi:.2f}"` ppm across the characterized region. That model resolves no
factor effect, so the measured figure is the one that bounds the result. Once the pure error
of the response is propagated, the upper bound of the 95 % predictive interval reaches the
criterion above elution buffer pH `{python} f"{par_lpa_ph_nor[1]:.3g}"`, which is why the
design space is capped there (@sec-par). At
the drug substance the attribute carries a capability of Cpk =
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['leached_protein_a','Cpk']:,.0f}"`, which is very large because the
polishing steps clear what capture introduces. Of the three attributes this step governs,
host cell protein has the tightest capability at Cpk =
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp','Cpk']:.2f}"`, with a mean of
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp','mean']:.1f}"` ng/mg against a limit of
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp','acc_high']:g}"` ng/mg.

`{python} f"{n_dev}"` deviations were recorded during execution. Both were investigated,
impact-assessed and dispositioned as retained, and neither altered a parameter
classification or the operating region defined in @sec-ds. They are described in @sec-dev.

No claim is made that this step assures the drug substance limit for host cell protein. The
capture pool carries `{python} f"{hcp_over_limit_sp:.0f}"` times that limit at the
set-point, and even the lowest value anywhere in the characterized region is
`{python} f"{hcp_over_limit_min:.0f}"` times it, so the cation and anion exchange steps
deliver the remaining clearance (PCR-007 and PCR-008). No viral clearance claim is made for
the Protein A step. Within those bounds the step is well understood over the ranges studied,
its operating region is defined, and its results roll up into PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose primary mechanism of action is
antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. It is produced by fed-batch cell culture and
purified by a platform train of six operations. Protein A capture is the first of those
operations, and it is followed by low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion
exchange, small-virus retentive filtration and ultrafiltration with diafiltration. The train
and the role of each step are described in PTP-001.

The step uses an immobilized Protein A resin operated in bind and elute mode. Clarified
harvest is loaded onto the equilibrated column, process impurities (host cell protein, DNA
and small molecules) pass into the flow through or are removed in the wash, and the antibody
is eluted with a low pH buffer. The elution pool is the feed to the low-pH hold, so the
elution buffer pH set here also conditions the following step. Capture therefore does three
things at once: it recovers the product, it removes the bulk of the impurity burden carried
out of cell culture, and it introduces a small amount of ligand released from the resin.

That released ligand is the quality attribute the step sets. Leached Protein A is a process
impurity of low to moderate criticality with an acceptance criterion of
`{python} f"{acc_lpa[0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{acc_lpa[1]:g}"` ppm (@tbl-cqa-set). Host cell
protein (HCP) and residual DNA are formed upstream and are reduced here, not set here. The
nominal batch leaves capture at `{python} f"{pa_hcp_nom:,.0f}"` ng/mg of host cell protein,
and residual DNA is reduced by `{python} f"{dna_lrv:.1f}"` log₁₀ across the step, so neither
attribute meets its drug substance criterion at this point in the train and neither is
expected to. The cross-step position is set out in @sec-control.

## Objectives

The objectives of the study were:

(i) to quantify the relationship between the operating parameters of the capture step and
    the responses that describe its product quality and process performance;
(ii) to define an operating region over which leached Protein A remains within its
     acceptance criterion and step yield remains acceptable;
(iii) to establish proven acceptable ranges for each characterized parameter and to
      confirm that the normal operating ranges sit inside them;
(iv) to classify each parameter against the criteria of SOP-4001; and
(v) to justify the ranges and controls carried into Stage 2 and into the control strategy
    for the drug substance.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The study is a Stage 1 process design activity in the sense of the lifecycle approach to
process validation [@fda2011]. Its content maps to the record that stage expects: the
sources of variability were identified, their effect on the responses was measured, and the
resulting understanding was converted into a control strategy. The enhanced development
approach of ICH Q8 provides the design-space framework, ICH Q11 the development and
manufacturing-process content, and ICH Q9 the risk methodology, under which criticality is
treated as a continuum and not as a binary label, following ICH Q9 itself and the A-Mab case
study [@amab2009].

No viral clearance is claimed for this step, so ICH Q5A is not applied here. Viral clearance
is claimed for low-pH inactivation, anion exchange and small-virus retentive filtration, and
is consolidated in PCMR-001. The paired protocol for this work is PCP-005, which fixed the
design, the acceptance criteria and the analysis before execution.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

Protein A capture is a well established operation in the Novacyte purification platform. The
same resin, the same buffer system and the same mode of operation have been used to
manufacture three earlier humanized IgG1 antibodies (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) and to supply
the A-Mab clinical programme, so the behaviour of the step is established from a large body
of performance history rather than from this study alone. Affinity capture is inherently
robust, because the separation rests on a specific interaction between the ligand and the Fc
region and not on a balance of weak forces that shifts with buffer composition. The purpose
of this study was therefore to confirm and bound known platform behaviour, not to discover
it.

The platform sets a clear mechanistic expectation for each parameter, and that expectation
framed the ranges. Pool HCP is expected to rise as protein load increases, because the mass
of co-adsorbed impurity carried into the elution pool grows with the mass of product bound.
Pool HCP is also expected to rise as elution buffer pH falls, because a more aggressive
elution desorbs species that are held less tightly than the antibody. Those two effects are
expected to interact, since the impurity available for desorption depends on how much
material was loaded. Step yield is expected to fall when a high load is combined with a high
linear velocity, because the contact time then becomes short relative to the rate of
binding. End of pool collect is expected to trade yield against pool volume and purity.

Leached Protein A is treated differently. Ligand release is a property of the resin, its
chemistry and its cycle history, and the low pH of the elution is the driver in principle.
The platform expectation was that release is small and roughly constant across the operating
window, and that its cycle-to-cycle variability is comparable to the precision of the assay.
This study was designed to test that expectation and not to assume it.

Prior knowledge is bounded in one respect that matters for the transfer. The platform
evidence covers the resin used in this characterization. An alternate Protein A resin was
assessed separately in RA-004 (`{python} PRIOR.loc['RA-004','date']`), which concluded that
independent characterization would be required and that bridging from platform data would
not be acceptable. Nothing in this report supports a resin change.

## Quality attributes in scope

The attribute this step sets is given in @tbl-cqa-set, and the attributes carried into the
step from upstream are given in @tbl-cqa-gov. Criticality follows the A-Mab Tool #1 assessment, in
which the impact of an attribute is combined with the uncertainty attached to it, and
attributes scoring high or very high are called critical [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
print("\n: The quality attribute set by the Protein A step, with its criticality from "
      "the A-Mab Tool #1 assessment. {#tbl-cqa-set}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["hcp", "residual_dna", "aggregates_hmw"]))
print("\n: Attributes carried into the Protein A step from upstream, which the step "
      "reduces or passes through. {#tbl-cqa-gov}")
```

Leached Protein A is the only entry in @tbl-cqa-set, and its criticality is low to moderate.
It is nonetheless carried in the register as a critical quality attribute, because the
register scores criticality as a continuum and does not drop an attribute that falls below
the threshold for the label. Two features of the attribute drive the study design. It is
introduced here and nowhere else, so no upstream control acts on it. It is also cleared by
the two ion exchange steps, so the level in the drug substance is not the level in the
capture pool.

Of the attributes in @tbl-cqa-gov, host cell protein is the one this step influences most,
and it is the response the multivariate design was built around. Residual DNA is of very low
criticality and is reduced by a fixed mechanism, since DNA does not bind the ligand and
passes into the flow through. Aggregates carry the highest criticality of the three in
@tbl-cqa-gov, but they are formed in the bioreactor and are not resolved by affinity
capture, so the step is treated as passing them through unchanged (their polish is the
subject of PCR-007).

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

RA-001 set the scope of this study before any of it was executed. The method there is risk
ranking and filtering: each parameter is scored for its potential impact on a quality
attribute and separately for its potential to interact with other parameters, and the
combined score decides the type of study it receives [@amab2009; @ichq9]. Parameters with no
plausible link to an attribute and a low interaction score are not studied and take their
ranges from the knowledge space (there are none of these at the capture step).

Four parameters were assigned to the multivariate design. Protein load and elution buffer pH
scored on the quality axis because both act on pool HCP, and both scored on the interaction
axis because the impurity mass available for desorption depends on the load. Load flow rate
and end of pool collect scored on process performance and not on product quality, and were
carried into the same design because the yield effect of flow depends on the load. Assigning
all four to one design is the reason the study can separate a load effect from a
load-by-flow effect.

Operating temperature and bed height were assigned to univariate assessment. Neither has a
mechanism by which it could change the chemistry of the separation over the range of
interest, since bed height acts through residence time (which is already varied through load
and flow) and operating temperature acts on binding kinetics only weakly over the range the
facility can produce. Both were nonetheless assessed across their characterization ranges,
because a parameter that is not studied cannot be given a proven acceptable range.

The ranges themselves were set at about twice the routine control range for each parameter,
following the platform convention for characterization studies. The wider ranges do two
things. They allow the study to see whether an effect that is invisible inside the NOR
appears at a distance from it, and they leave room to move the operating point later without
a new study.

# Materials and methods {#sec-mm}

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The characterization was executed on a qualified laboratory-scale model of the commercial
capture step, operated under SOP-2007 and qualified under SOP-1001. The model was designed
on the established principles of chromatography scaling: bed height is held at the
commercial value of `{python} f"{P.param('bed_height').setpoint:g}"`
`{python} P.param('bed_height').unit`, linear velocity is matched in cm/hr, protein load is
matched in g of product per L of resin, and the equilibration, wash and elution volumes are
matched as column volumes. Column efficiency was verified by plate count and peak asymmetry
before each execution.

Qualification compared the small-scale system against commercial-equivalent runs on the
inputs and the outputs that matter to this step (step yield, pool volume, pool host cell
protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A), and no statistically significant difference in
column efficiency or in any performance measure was found between the two scales. The
qualification data are held in the SOP-1001 qualification record for the capture model and
are not reproduced here. On that basis the model is treated as representative of the
commercial step, and the operating ranges and clearance claimed below are claimed for the
commercial step through it.

Two features of the model bound what it can support. It reproduces the hydrodynamics and the
chemistry of the separation, but it does not reproduce the resin cycle history of a
commercial campaign, so all runs were executed on resin within the early part of its
validated life. It also uses a single representative clarified harvest as the feed, so the
study varies this step's parameters and not the properties of the material entering it. The
consequence of both bounds is stated in @sec-discussion.

The runs were executed in the temperature-controlled chromatography chamber EQ-CHR-118,
which was `{python} EQ.loc['EQ-CHR-118','Calibration status']` and whose next calibration
was due `{python} EQ.loc['EQ-CHR-118','Next calibration due']`.

## Operation

Each run followed the commercial sequence. The column was equilibrated, loaded to the target
protein load at the target linear velocity, washed, and eluted with the low pH elution
buffer, and collection started on the ascending edge of the elution peak and stopped at the
target end of pool collect, expressed in column volumes. The pool was sampled, then titrated
and held for the low-pH inactivation step. Set-points and ranges are given in @tbl-params.

Buffers were prepared and released under SOP-2103
(`{python} PRIOR.loc['SOP-2103','title']`), and each elution buffer
lot was released on measured pH before use (see @sec-dev). Resin packing, sanitization and
cycle accounting follow SOP-2008. Resin cycle number was held constant across the study and
was not a factor of the design.

## Analytical methods

Each of the two impurity responses is measured by one validated method. Pool host cell
protein is measured by the ELISA validated under AMV-3012. Leached Protein A is measured by
the ELISA validated under AMV-3016. Size variants are measured by SEC-HPLC (AMV-3011) and
residual DNA by qPCR (AMV-3014). Both support the in-process panel and neither is a response
of the multivariate design. Step yield is determined by protein mass balance across the step
under SOP-2007. The validated performance of the two ELISA methods is given in @tbl-methods
in Appendix D.

Two points about method performance carry into the interpretation of the results. The
leached Protein A ELISA has an intermediate precision of
`{python} f"{MPERF.loc['AMV-3016','Precision (%RSD)']:g}"` %RSD and a limit of
quantitation of `{python} MPERF.loc['AMV-3016','LOQ']`, so results in the low single digits
are quantitative but not sharp, and the host cell protein ELISA has an intermediate
precision of `{python} f"{MPERF.loc['AMV-3012','Precision (%RSD)']:g}"` %RSD. Where a
centre-point spread reported below is larger than these figures, the excess is run-to-run
process variation and is treated as such. Where it is smaller, the spread lies within the
validated precision of the method, and no process contribution can be separated from assay
noise on the replicates available.

## Sampling plan

One elution pool sample was taken per run and assayed for host cell protein and leached
Protein A. Load and flow-through samples were taken on every run to close the mass balance
and to confirm the input to the step. Replication is carried by the centre points rather
than by repeat assays: the screening design carries `{python} f"{cp_scr}"` centre-point runs
and the response-surface design carries `{python} f"{cp_rsm}"` (Appendix A and Appendix B).
Those replicates are independent executions at the set-point, so their spread contains both
the process and the assay contribution, and they provide the pure-error term for the
lack-of-fit tests in @sec-results.

## Statistical methods

Factors are analysed in coded units, in which the set-point is 0 and the edges of the
characterization range are the two coded extremes (−1 and +1). Coding makes the effect
estimates comparable across parameters with different units, and it means an effect is read
as the change in the response between the centre of the range and its edge.

The screening design is analysed as an ordinary least-squares model in the main effects and
the two-factor interactions. An effect is reported as twice the coded coefficient, so that
it is the change across the whole characterization range. The response-surface design is
analysed as a full quadratic model in the same coded factors. Significance is assessed at α
= `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` throughout, and no term is removed from a reported model on the
basis of its p-value.

Model adequacy is judged on four things together: the coefficient of determination with its
adjusted and predicted values, the overall F test, and an ANOVA partition of the residual
into lack of fit and pure error (tested against the centre-point replicates). The predicted
value is computed by leave-one-out prediction, so a model that fits its own data and
predicts a held-out run poorly is visible. A response for which no term is significant is
reported as robust to the factors over the ranges studied, and the factors are retained in
the knowledge space as evidence of that robustness.

Proven acceptable ranges are computed from the fitted response-surface model in two ways, as
PCP-005 specifies. The first holds the other parameters at their set-points and scans the
parameter of interest across its characterization range. The second propagates the normal
operating ranges of the other parameters by Monte-Carlo of the fitted model, and keeps the
part of the range over which the upper bound of the 95 % predictive interval still meets the
criterion. Commercial-scale capability is estimated by Monte-Carlo of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches with every parameter varying inside its NOR,
and is reported as a one-sided Cpk against the drug substance criterion.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

The design resolves the active factors and then maps the region they define. @tbl-params
gives every parameter with its set-point, its normal operating range, the range studied and
the classification the study produced. The coded letters used in the effect and coefficient
tables are given in @tbl-legend.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(PARAMS)
print("\n: Parameters of the Protein A step, with the ranges studied and the "
      "classification resulting from this study. {#tbl-params}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
print("\n: Coded factor legend for the screening and response-surface designs. "
      "{#tbl-legend}")
```

The characterization range in @tbl-params is the knowledge space of this step, not a proven
acceptable range. Each range is about twice the corresponding NOR, and each was chosen
against a mechanism. Protein load spans `{python} f"{P.param('load').prange[0]:g}"` to
`{python} f"{P.param('load').prange[1]:g}"` `{python} P.param('load').unit`, which reaches
well past the point at which the platform expects the impurity carried into the pool to
grow, while staying below the static binding capacity of the resin. Elution buffer pH spans
`{python} f"{P.param('elution_ph').prange[0]:g}"` to
`{python} f"{P.param('elution_ph').prange[1]:g}"`. The low edge was set above the pH at
which antibody precipitation becomes a risk during elution, and the high edge was set at the
point where elution becomes incomplete. Load flow rate spans
`{python} f"{P.param('flow').prange[0]:g}"` to
`{python} f"{P.param('flow').prange[1]:g}"` `{python} P.param('flow').unit`, which covers
the range of linear velocities the commercial skid can deliver at this bed height, and end
of pool collect spans `{python} f"{P.param('end_collect').prange[0]:g}"` to
`{python} f"{P.param('end_collect').prange[1]:g}"`
`{python} P.param('end_collect').unit`, from a cut that sacrifices yield to one that
collects deep into the descending edge.

## Screening design

The screening study was a two-level full factorial in the four multivariate parameters,
augmented with centre points. It comprised `{python} f"{n_scr}"` runs in total:
`{python} f"{n_scr_fact}"` factorial runs and `{python} f"{cp_scr}"` replicated centre
points. The design estimates all four main effects and all six two-factor interactions
without aliasing, and the centre points give an independent estimate of pure error and a
test for curvature (a two-level design cannot separate curvature from the mean without
them). The full design matrix with the measured responses is given in Appendix A.

The purpose of this design is to identify which factors have an important statistical effect
on each response. It is not the predictive model. A two-level design carries no information
about curvature within the range it spans, so the magnitude of an effect it estimates is
refined by the response-surface study that follows.

## Response-surface design

All four screening factors were carried into the response-surface study, because the
screening results left none of them without an effect on at least one response. The design
is a face-centred central composite design of `{python} f"{n_rsm}"` runs:
`{python} f"{n_rsm_fact}"` factorial runs, `{python} f"{n_rsm_ax}"` axial runs on the faces
of the cube and `{python} f"{cp_rsm}"` replicated centre points. Placing the axial points on
the faces keeps every run inside the characterization ranges, which matters here because
those ranges are also the edges of the knowledge space. The design supports the full
quadratic model of `{python} f"{n_rsm_terms}"` terms and leaves residual degrees of freedom
for the lack-of-fit test. The matrix and the responses are given in Appendix B.

This is the predictive model of the step and the basis of the design space in @sec-ds.

## Univariate assessment

Operating temperature and bed height were assessed one parameter at a time across the ranges
given in @tbl-params, with the remaining parameters at their set-points. Pool host cell
protein, leached Protein A and step yield were measured on each run (the same responses as
the multivariate design). Neither parameter was linked to a quality attribute, and both were
classified as general process parameters on that basis (@sec-class). The supporting data are
held in the study data package referenced by PCP-005.

No response surface was fitted for either parameter, so no multivariate claim is made for
them. Their acceptable ranges are the ranges assessed, and they are not part of the region
defined in @sec-ds.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility

Reproducibility at the set-point differs sharply between the three responses, and it sets
what each of the models below can be expected to resolve. @tbl-cvrsm gives the centre-point
mean, standard deviation and coefficient of variation for the response-surface design, and
@tbl-cvscr gives the same for the screening design.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm"))
print(f"\n: Centre-point reproducibility in the response-surface design, from "
      f"{cp_rsm} replicated runs at the set-point. {{#tbl-cvrsm}}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.center_cv_df(UO, "screening"))
print("\n: Centre-point reproducibility in the screening design. {#tbl-cvscr}")
```

Step yield is the most reproducible response, at
`{python} f"{cv_r.loc[LBL[YLD],'%CV']:.1f}"` % in the response-surface design. Pool HCP
reproduces to
`{python} f"{cv_r.loc[LBL[HCP],'%CV']:.1f}"` % there, which is well inside the effects
reported below. Leached Protein A is the least reproducible response, at
`{python} f"{cv_r.loc[LBL[LPA],'%CV']:.1f}"` % across the response-surface centre points
and `{python} f"{cv_s.loc[LBL[LPA],'%CV']:.1f}"` % across the screening centre points, and
that spread is several times the intermediate precision of AMV-3016, so most of it is
run-to-run variation in the amount of ligand released and not assay noise. A response with
this much pure error can only resolve a large effect, which is the correct context for the
leached Protein A results below.

Pool HCP behaves differently in the two designs. Its screening centre points give
`{python} f"{cv_s.loc[LBL[HCP],'%CV']:.1f}"` % against
`{python} f"{cv_r.loc[LBL[HCP],'%CV']:.1f}"` % in the response-surface design, on
`{python} f"{cp_scr}"` and `{python} f"{cp_rsm}"` replicates. The screening figure is above
the `{python} f"{MPERF.loc['AMV-3012','Precision (%RSD)']:g}"` %RSD intermediate precision
validated for AMV-3012 and the response-surface figure is well below it, so the two designs
give different accounts of how reproducible this response is. Each design supplies the pure
error for its own lack-of-fit test, so the wider screening spread does not enter the
response-surface tests in @sec-rsm.

The centre points also give the pure-error term used in every lack-of-fit test in this
section. They are independent executions at the set-point and not repeat injections of one
sample, so their spread is intended to carry the process contribution as well as the assay
contribution. For pool HCP in the response-surface design that cannot be shown, because the
spread is smaller than the validated precision of the method that measured it. A pure-error
estimate on `{python} f"{cp_rsm - 1}"` degrees of freedom is imprecise in both directions,
and the lack-of-fit result for pool HCP below passes by a narrow margin, so the two should
be read together.

## Screening: factor effects

The screening design separated the active factors for pool HCP and for step yield, and found
none for leached Protein A. @tbl-scrfit gives the model summary for the three responses.

```{python}
#| output: asis

print("\n: Screening model summary. The model for leached Protein A is not significant "
      "overall. {#tbl-scrfit}")
```

The two significant models in @tbl-scrfit behave very differently from the third (leached
Protein A). Pool HCP and step yield are both fitted with R² above
`{python} f"{min(fit_s[HCP]['R2'], fit_s[YLD]['R2']):.2f}"` and overall p-values below
`{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"`. The leached Protein A model has an overall p-value of
`{python} f"{fit_s[LPA]['p']:.2f}"` and a negative adjusted R², which is what a model
returns when its terms explain less than the degrees of freedom they consume, and no factor
effect on leached Protein A was resolved by the screening design.

Pool HCP is driven by elution buffer pH and protein load, and by the interaction between
them (@tbl-scr-hcp). Lowering elution buffer pH across the range raises pool HCP by
`{python} f"{abs(D.screening_effects_df(UO, HCP).iloc[0]['Effect']):,.0f}"` ng/mg, which is
the largest effect estimated for this response. Raising protein load across its range raises
pool HCP by `{python} f"{abs(D.screening_effects_df(UO, HCP).iloc[1]['Effect']):,.0f}"`
ng/mg. The load by elution pH interaction is significant and negative, so the penalty from a
high load is smaller when the elution is milder. Neither load flow rate nor end of pool
collect reached significance for this response
(p > `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` for both).

```{python}

show(D.screening_effects_df(UO, HCP, top=5))
print("\n: Largest screening effects on pool HCP. The full table is in Appendix C. "
      "{#tbl-scr-hcp}")
```

Step yield is driven by end of pool collect, and then by protein load and load flow rate
(@tbl-scr-yield). Collecting further into the descending edge of the elution peak raises
yield by `{python} pct(abs(D.screening_effects_df(UO, YLD).iloc[0]['Effect']))` across the
range, which is the dominant term. Load and flow each reduce yield, and their interaction is
significant, so the two act together and not separately. The remaining interactions that
reach significance are small and are reported for completeness in Appendix C.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.screening_effects_df(UO, YLD, top=5))
print("\n: Largest screening effects on step yield. The full table is in Appendix C. "
      "{#tbl-scr-yield}")
```

These are identifications, not predictions. The screening design places every run at an edge
or at the centre, so it can say which factors matter and in which direction, but it cannot
describe how a response bends between those points. The magnitudes above are refined by the
response-surface models in @sec-rsm, and the design space rests on those models and not on
this one.

The response-surface study confirms the screening result for pool HCP and for step yield,

(p = `{python} f"{fit_r[LPA]['p']:.2f}"`) and its predicted R² is negative, so no

The coefficient table for pool HCP is given in @tbl-rsm-hcp, and the ANOVA partition with

Four terms of @tbl-rsm-hcp carry most of the surface. Elution buffer pH has the largest
coefficient, protein load the second largest, and the interaction between them is
significant and negative as it was in the screening study. The quadratic term in elution
buffer pH is significant and positive, which is the curvature the screening design could not
detect: pool HCP falls steeply as pH rises from the low edge and then flattens. End of pool
collect (term D) also carries a significant negative coefficient, at
`{python} pct(d_over_b)` of the elution pH coefficient in magnitude. Its effect on this
response is real and it is small.

Two smaller interactions also reach `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"`. Protein load with end of pool
collect and elution buffer pH with end of pool collect carry `{python} pct(ad_over_ab)` and
`{python} pct(bd_over_ab)` of the load by elution pH coefficient in magnitude. Both are
reported in @tbl-rsm-hcp and neither is interpreted further here. Both involve end of pool
collect, which is held at its set-point in the surfaces shown below, so neither contributes
to those panels.

The lack-of-fit test in @tbl-anova-hcp does not reject the model
(p = `{python} f"{fit_r[HCP]['p_lof']:.3f}"`), but the margin above
`{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` is narrow. The pure-error term comes from only
`{python} f"{cp_rsm}"` centre points, so the test has little power, and a narrow pass
should not be read as a demonstration that the quadratic form is complete. The diagnostics
in @fig-diag-hcp support the model on the other axes. Standardized residuals show no
structure against the predicted value, the normal quantile plot is close to linear, and the
actual against predicted plot sits on the identity line across the whole range of the
response.

ng/mg between the lowest and the highest load. At the high pH edge the same change in load
moves it from `{python} f"{hcp_hi_ph[0]:,.0f}"` to `{python} f"{hcp_hi_ph[1]:,.0f}"` ng/mg,

ng/mg at the low pH edge than at the high one. The step yield panel is almost
flat in this plane, which is correct, since yield is governed by end of pool collect and by

Protein A panel is shown for completeness. The model behind it is not significant overall,
and the one term in it that reaches `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` is discussed below.

```{python}
#| label: fig-contours
```

The coefficient tables for step yield and for leached Protein A are given in Appendix C. For
step yield the pattern of the screening study is reproduced: end of pool collect carries the
largest coefficient, protein load and load flow rate carry smaller negative coefficients,
and the load by flow interaction remains significant. For leached Protein A the only term
reaching `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` is the quadratic in elution buffer pH. Since the model
containing it is not significant overall, and since
`{python} f"{n_rsm_terms - 1}"` terms were tested in it, that single term is not treated as
a demonstrated effect. It is carried into the proven acceptable range analysis in @sec-par
because doing so is conservative, and it is identified there as the reason one range is
bounded.

## Mechanistic interpretation

The shape of the pool HCP surface follows from how the two mechanisms of impurity carryover
combine. Host cell protein reaches the elution pool by two routes: it is co-adsorbed onto
the resin and the antibody during the load, and it is desorbed with the antibody when the pH
drops. Protein load controls the first route (co-adsorption), because more product bound
means more associated impurity retained through the wash. Elution buffer pH controls the
second, because a lower pH breaks weaker interactions as well as the specific one. The
interaction term is negative because the second route gates the first: impurity that was
co-adsorbed only reaches the pool if the elution is aggressive enough to release it.

The positive curvature in elution buffer pH has the same explanation. Between the low edge
of the range and about the set-point, each further drop in pH releases another population of
weakly held species, so the response is steep. Above the set-point the elution is already
selective and the remaining species stay on the column, so the response flattens. This
reproduces the behaviour reported for the capture step in the published case study
[@amab2009].

End of pool collect acts on the same quantity from the other side. Pool host cell protein is
expressed per mg of product, so a later cut that adds product mass to the denominator lowers
the ratio, and the coefficient for that term in @tbl-rsm-hcp is negative. The platform
expectation recorded in @sec-prior was that a later cut trades purity for yield. Over the
ranges studied the data do not support that for this response, and the sign of the effect is
the opposite one.

Step yield is governed by two unrelated mechanisms and the surface shows both. End of pool
collect is a simple integration effect, because product continues to elute on the descending
edge and a later cut recovers more of it (at the cost of a larger pool). The load by flow
interaction is a mass transfer effect. At a high load the binding front reaches further down
the bed, and at a high linear velocity the contact time in that front is shorter, so product
breaks through into the flow through before it can bind. Neither mechanism touches product
quality, which is why both parameters classify on process consistency in @sec-class.

Leached Protein A behaved as the platform predicted. Ligand release is set by the chemistry
of the resin and by its cycle history, both of which were held constant, and the elution pH
range studied here is not wide enough to move it against the run-to-run variability of the
step. The null result is informative in two ways. It means the amount of ligand entering the
process does not have to be managed by choosing an operating point inside this region, and
it means the four factors stay in the knowledge space as evidence that the attribute is
robust to them across the ranges studied.

Taken together, these mechanisms are why the operating region has to be multivariate and not
a set of four independent ranges. `{python} f"{n_sig_2fi}"` of the significant terms in
@tbl-rsm-hcp are interactions, so the acceptable range of protein load is not a fixed
interval. It depends on where elution buffer pH sits. A set of one-dimensional ranges cannot
express that, and the design space in @sec-ds is stated as a region for exactly this reason.

# Design space {#sec-ds}

The design space of the capture step is the characterized region in the four multivariate
parameters, bounded above in elution buffer pH by the robustness limit derived in @sec-par.
Inside that region the attribute this step sets stays within its acceptance criterion when
the other parameters move anywhere within their normal operating ranges, and step yield
stays above the value given below. The region is defined on the fitted response-surface
models of @sec-rsm and not on the screening study.

Two planes carry the structure of the region. The plane of protein load against elution
buffer pH is the plane in which pool HCP moves, and it is the plane shown in @fig-contours.
The plane of protein load against load flow rate is the plane in which step yield moves. The
two planes are almost independent of each other, since elution buffer pH has no significant
effect on yield and load flow rate has none on pool HCP.

The corners and the region extremes below are computed over the full characterization ranges
of @tbl-params, which is the wider of the two regions and the conservative one to quote. The
design space itself is that region with elution buffer pH capped at
`{python} f"{par_lpa_ph_nor[1]:.3g}"`, and capping it lowers the highest predicted leached
Protein A from `{python} f"{reg_lpa_hi:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{reg_lpa_hi_cap:.2f}"` ppm. The
lowest predicted step yield is the same figure either way, because elution buffer pH carries
no significant effect on yield.

The worst case corner for pool HCP is `{python} corner_str(hcp_corner)`, with all four
parameters at an edge of their characterization ranges. There the fitted model predicts
`{python} f"{hcp_hi:,.0f}"` ng/mg against
`{python} f"{hcp_sp:,.0f}"` ng/mg at the set-point and `{python} f"{hcp_lo:,.0f}"` ng/mg at the
lowest corner, so the step spans more than an order of magnitude in pool HCP across the
region it was characterized over. That corner is not excluded from the design space, because
pool HCP is not an acceptance criterion at this step. What follows from it is a requirement
on the downstream steps, and that is stated in @sec-control.

The worst case corner for leached Protein A is `{python} corner_str(lpa_corner)`, at which
the model predicts `{python} f"{lpa_hi:.2f}"` ppm. The highest mean anywhere in the region,
corners and interior together, is `{python} f"{reg_lpa_hi:.2f}"` ppm against an acceptance
criterion of `{python} f"{acc_lpa[1]:g}"` ppm. Those are mean levels from a model that
resolves no factor effect, so the measured results bound the attribute better than the model
does. The highest leached Protein A measured in either design is
`{python} f"{lpa_corner_obs:.2f}"` ppm, on response-surface run
`{python} f"{lpa_corner_run}"`, which is that same corner (@tbl-appb2).

The worst case corner for step yield is
`{python} corner_str(yld_corner)`, at which the model predicts
`{python} pct(yld_lo)` against `{python} pct(yld_sp)` at the set-point, and the lowest
value anywhere in the region is `{python} pct(reg_yld_lo)`.

The normal operating ranges in @tbl-params sit inside this region with margin on every
parameter. Propagating them through the fitted models gives pool HCP between
`{python} f"{nor_hcp_lo:,.0f}"` and `{python} f"{nor_hcp_hi:,.0f}"` ng/mg, leached Protein A
at or below `{python} f"{nor_lpa_hi:.2f}"` ppm, and step yield at or above
`{python} pct(nor_yld_lo)`. The nesting is the usual one. The characterization ranges are
the knowledge space, the region defined here is the design space, and the normal operating
ranges are the control space the process is actually run in.

Movement within the design space is not a change in the sense of ICH Q8. It is still subject
to the site change-management system under ICH Q10, and a planned move is assessed
prospectively against the risks of that particular move. Movement outside the design space
requires change control and, where the move is outside the characterization ranges, new
data.

Three bounds apply to this claim. The region is defined only over the ranges in @tbl-params;
nothing here supports a setting outside them. The models predict mean levels, so the
assurance at the edge of the region is lower than at its centre, and the capability figures
in @sec-cap are the statement of assurance inside the NOR and not at the edge. The region is
defined on a qualified scale-down model with resin early in its validated life and a single
representative feed, so it is claimed for the commercial step through the qualification
described in @sec-mm and no further.

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

The acceptance basis has to be stated before the ranges, because it differs between the two
governed attributes. Both criteria in this section are the study-provided drug substance
specifications: `{python} f"{acc_lpa[0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{acc_lpa[1]:g}"` ppm for leached
Protein A and `{python} f"{acc_hcp[0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{acc_hcp[1]:g}"` ng/mg for host cell
protein. Neither is an in-process limit for the capture pool, and no viral clearance
response arises at this step, so no step-level criterion is back-calculated anywhere in this
report. Step yield has no acceptance criterion of this kind and is reported as process
performance.

@tbl-par gives, for each governed attribute and each multivariate parameter, the
characterization range and both proven acceptable ranges: the range proven with the other
parameters at their set-points, and the range proven with the other parameters varying
inside their normal operating ranges.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.par_table(UO))
print("\n: Proven acceptable ranges by attribute and parameter, from the fitted "
      "response-surface models. {#tbl-par}")
```

For leached Protein A the whole characterization range of protein load, load flow rate and
end of pool collect is proven acceptable under both analyses, which means each of those
ranges stays acceptable when the other three parameters move anywhere inside their normal
operating ranges. Elution buffer pH is the one exception. Its at set-point range is the full
`{python} f"{par_lpa_ph_sp[0]:.3g}"`–`{python} f"{par_lpa_ph_sp[1]:.3g}"`, and the
NOR-propagated range stops at `{python} f"{par_lpa_ph_nor[1]:.3g}"`. The binding attribute
is leached Protein A and the binding statistic is the upper bound of the 95 % predictive
interval, which reaches the acceptance criterion near the top of the pH range once the pure
error of the response is propagated with it. The NOR upper edge for this parameter is
`{python} f"{P.param('elution_ph').nor[1]:g}"`, so the routine operating range sits inside
the proven range with margin.

That bound should be read with caution. It comes from the quadratic term discussed in
@sec-rsm, in a model that is not significant overall, combined with a pure error of
`{python} f"{cv_r.loc[LBL[LPA],'%CV']:.1f}"` % at the centre point. It is therefore a
conservative limit produced by an imprecise response, and not a demonstrated edge of
failure. @fig-par-lpa shows the analysis for the governing parameter of this attribute,
which is `{python} P.param(gov_lpa).name.lower()`. The acceptable region is shaded, and the
response sits below the criterion across the whole range in both panels.

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-lpa
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for leached Protein A against its governing parameter, at set-point (left) and with the other parameters varying within their NOR (right). The acceptable region is shaded green and the acceptance limit is drawn."
D.fig_par(UO, LPA, gov_lpa)
plt.show()
```

For pool HCP no proven acceptable range is returned for any parameter under either analysis,
and the reason is that the capture pool does not meet the drug substance limit at any
setting studied. At the set-point the model predicts `{python} f"{hcp_sp:,.0f}"` ng/mg
against a criterion of `{python} f"{acc_hcp[1]:g}"` ng/mg, and the lowest value anywhere in
the region is `{python} f"{reg_hcp_lo:,.0f}"` ng/mg. @fig-par-hcp shows this directly: the
acceptance limit lies below the plotted response across the whole range of
`{python} P.param(gov_hcp).name.lower()`, so no region is shaded.

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-hcp
#| fig-cap: "Pool HCP against its governing parameter, at set-point (left) and with the other parameters varying within their NOR (right). The drug substance acceptance limit lies below the response everywhere, so no acceptable region is shaded."
D.fig_par(UO, HCP, gov_hcp)
plt.show()
```

This is the expected result for a capture step and not an adverse finding about it. Host
cell protein is cleared by three chromatography steps in series, and the criterion applies
to the drug substance and not to an intermediate pool. Since the cation and anion exchange
steps reduce host cell protein to acceptable and consistent levels, the acceptable pool HCP
leaving capture is linked to the operating conditions of those steps and cannot be fixed
here in isolation. The linkage is made in PCR-007 and PCR-008 and consolidated in PCMR-001,
and the drug substance outcome is reported in @sec-cap.

The relationship between this section and @sec-ds should be read one way only. The proven
acceptable ranges here are univariate statements, one parameter at a time, and the
NOR-propagated column is a robustness statement about that same univariate range. The design
space is the multivariate region. Where a whole characterization range is proven acceptable,
as it is for three of the four parameters, the binding constraint on the operating region is
not that univariate range at all; it is the corner of the multivariate region, which is why
@sec-ds names the corners. Every range in @tbl-par is bounded by the characterization ranges
and by the fitted model, and none of them extends beyond the region the study covered.

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-cap}

Commercial-scale capability was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches with every process parameter varying inside
its normal operating range. @tbl-cap gives the result for the three attributes this step
governs, as a one-sided Cpk against the drug substance criterion.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_for(CAPK))
print("\n: Commercial-scale capability at the drug substance for the attributes the "
      "Protein A step governs. {#tbl-cap}")
```

Host cell protein has the tightest capability of the three, at Cpk =
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp','Cpk']:.2f}"`, with a simulated mean of
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp','mean']:.1f}"` ng/mg against a limit of
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp','acc_high']:g}"` ng/mg, so the margin to the limit is
`{python} f"{hcp_sigma_margin:.0f}"` standard deviations of the batch-to-batch
distribution. That capability is a property of the three clearance steps acting in series
and not of capture alone. This step's contribution is the principal clearance of host cell
protein from clarified harvest, and the polishing steps are reported in PCR-007 and PCR-008.

Leached Protein A and residual DNA are far from their criteria at the drug substance, at Cpk
= `{python} f"{CAPR.loc['leached_protein_a','Cpk']:,.0f}"` and
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['residual_dna','Cpk']:.1f}"` respectively. A capability index of that
size is not a useful discriminator and should not be read as one. The informative statement
for leached Protein A is the level in the capture pool itself, before any downstream
clearance is credited: `{python} f"{lpa_sp:.2f}"` ppm at the set-point and no more than
`{python} f"{nor_lpa_hi:.2f}"` ppm anywhere inside the normal operating ranges, against a
criterion of `{python} f"{acc_lpa[1]:g}"` ppm. The attribute the step sets is in
specification at the point it is created.

Step yield is a process performance measure and carries no capability index (there is no
acceptance criterion of that kind to compute one against). Inside the normal operating
ranges the fitted model predicts a yield of at least
`{python} pct(nor_yld_lo)`, against `{python} pct(yld_sp)` at the set-point. The nominal
batch recovered `{python} pct(float(PS.loc[P.step, 'step_yield']))` across this step.

Two bounds apply to every figure in this section. All of them are estimated from qualified
scale-down models with parameters varying inside their NORs, so they describe the process as
it is intended to be run and not its behaviour at the edges of the design space. All of them
are predictions to be confirmed at commercial scale during Stage 2. The lowest capability
anywhere in the drug substance process is Cpk =
`{python} f"{V['min_cpk']:.2f}"`, which belongs to a viral clearance attribute set at
another step and is reported in PCMR-001.

# Parameter classification {#sec-class}

Each parameter was classified under SOP-4001 from its demonstrated effect and from the risk
that it leaves the design space in routine operation. The resulting classes are in
@tbl-params, and the reasoning for each is below.

- Protein load is a well-controlled critical process parameter. It has a significant
  effect on pool HCP and interacts with elution buffer pH, so it is linked to a quality
  attribute. It is set by mass balance from a measured load concentration and column volume,
  which makes an excursion outside the design space unlikely, so it is classified as well
  controlled and not as critical.
- Elution buffer pH is a well-controlled critical process parameter. It carries the
  largest effect on pool HCP of any parameter studied, it is the source of the only
  curvature that reaches significance, and it also conditions the feed to the low-pH inactivation step. It is
  nonetheless easy to control: each buffer lot is released on measured pH and the elution is
  monitored in line. The deviation described in @sec-dev shows why that release test
  matters.
- Load flow rate is a key process parameter. Its effect on pool HCP does not reach
  significance in the predictive model (p = `{python} f"{p_flow_hcp:.3f}"` in
  @tbl-rsm-hcp), which is marginal and is not treated as a demonstrated effect, and it has
  no significant effect on leached Protein A (@tbl-appc5). Its effect on step yield is
  significant both alone and through its interaction with protein load (@tbl-appc4). It is
  controlled for process consistency and not for product quality.
- End of pool collect is a key process parameter. It carries the largest effect on step
  yield of any parameter in the study, and it also has a significant effect on pool HCP, at
  `{python} pct(d_over_b)` of the elution pH coefficient in magnitude, and pool HCP is
  controlled to its drug substance criterion by the downstream polishing steps and not
  here. It is therefore classified on process consistency.
- Operating temperature is a general process parameter. The univariate assessment
  linked it to no quality attribute across its characterization range, and no mechanism is
  known by which it could affect the affinity interaction over that range.
- Bed height is a general process parameter. It was assessed univariately, it is linked
  to no quality attribute, and its effect on the separation acts through residence time,
  which is already characterized through protein load and load flow rate.

Two of these classifications rest on a null result, and both null results are kept rather
than dropped. Operating temperature and bed height stay in the knowledge space with their
characterization ranges attached, as evidence that the step is robust to them over those
ranges. The same applies to load flow rate and end of pool collect with respect to product
quality. Neither acts on the attribute this step sets, and the effect end of pool collect
carries on pool HCP is small and is managed by the downstream polishing steps, so both are
classified on process consistency and their ranges are justified on that basis.

The summary is `{python} f"{n_wccpp}"` well-controlled critical process parameters,
`{python} f"{n_kpp}"` key process parameters and `{python} f"{n_gpp}"` general process
parameters, and `{python} f"{n_cpp}"` critical process parameters. No parameter at this step
requires the most stringent class. That outcome matches the platform history. Affinity
capture is an inherently robust separation, and the two quality-linked parameters are both
measured directly before use.

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-control}

The capture step contributes five things to the drug substance control strategy.

First, it controls the two quality-linked parameters to the normal operating ranges in
@tbl-params: protein load to
`{python} f"{P.param('load').nor[0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{P.param('load').nor[1]:g}"`
`{python} P.param('load').unit` and elution buffer pH to
`{python} f"{P.param('elution_ph').nor[0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{P.param('elution_ph').nor[1]:g}"`.
Both ranges sit inside the design space of @sec-ds with margin, and both parameters are
verified before use rather than inferred afterwards.

Second, it controls the two key process parameters, load flow rate and end of pool collect,
to their normal operating ranges for process consistency, since neither is linked to a
quality attribute and both are included because holding them makes the step's yield and pool
volume predictable for the operations that follow.

Third, it carries in-process controls on the elution pool. Pool host cell protein and
leached Protein A are measured on every batch (AMV-3012 and AMV-3016), and step yield is
closed by mass balance. These are monitoring points and not acceptance limits at this step,
and they are the input the downstream clearance credit is taken against.

Fourth, it carries life-cycle controls on the resin. Packing, sanitization and cycle
accounting run under SOP-2008, and the characterization reported here was executed on resin
early in its validated life (cycle number was held constant across the study). A change of
resin is outside this control strategy and would require independent characterization under
RA-004.

Fifth, it carries a material control that follows directly from @sec-dev. Each elution
buffer lot is released on measured pH before use, because elution buffer pH is the parameter
with the largest effect on pool HCP and a preparation error is not otherwise detectable
until the pool is assayed.

The step does not control host cell protein to its drug substance criterion, and the control
strategy does not claim that it does. The nominal batch leaves capture at
`{python} f"{pa_hcp_nom:,.0f}"` ng/mg. Cation exchange then reduces host cell protein by a
factor of `{python} f"{cex_fold:.0f}"` and anion exchange by a further factor of
`{python} f"{aex_fold:.1f}"`, giving `{python} f"{ds_hcp_nom:.1f}"` ng/mg at the drug
substance for that batch. The mean across the
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` simulated batches of @tbl-cap is
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp','mean']:.1f}"` ng/mg, since the simulation varies every
parameter inside its normal operating range and the nominal batch is a single point in that
distribution. Those credits belong to PCR-007 and PCR-008. The step likewise makes no viral
clearance claim. Clearance across affinity capture is well documented for this class of
process [@amab2009], but the modular claim for A-Mab rests on low-pH inactivation, anion
exchange and small-virus retentive filtration, and it is consolidated in PCMR-001 [@ichq5a].

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The capture step is well understood over the ranges studied, and the understanding is
concentrated in one relationship. Pool host cell protein is governed by elution buffer pH
and protein load together, with a significant interaction and significant curvature in pH,
and the response-surface model describes that relationship well enough to predict a held-out
run. Everything else the study found is either a process performance effect or a null
result. That is a simple outcome for a step of this importance, and it is consistent with
the platform history summarized in @sec-prior.

The result that most constrains what can be claimed is the leached Protein A model. The
attribute this step sets is the one for which no factor effect could be resolved, and the
reason is visible in the centre points: pure error of
`{python} f"{cv_r.loc[LBL[LPA],'%CV']:.1f}"` % leaves little room for a real effect to
emerge. The conclusion is not that the operating parameters cannot influence ligand release.
It is that they do not influence it enough to be seen against the step's own run-to-run
variation across the ranges studied, which is the more useful statement for a control
strategy and the weaker one for a mechanistic claim.

Confidence in the scale-down model rests on the qualification described in @sec-mm and on
the agreement between the fitted effects and the platform expectation. The agreement is
closer on the effects than on the absolute level. The centre-point mean for pool HCP in the
response-surface design is `{python} f"{cp_hcp_mean:,.0f}"` ng/mg, against
`{python} f"{pa_hcp_nom:,.0f}"` ng/mg for the nominal batch at commercial equivalent
conditions. That difference is small beside the `{python} f"{hcp_span_fold:.0f}"`-fold span
the model covers across the characterized region, and it is larger than the scatter of the
centre points themselves (standard deviation `{python} f"{cp_hcp_sd:,.0f}"` ng/mg on
`{python} f"{cp_rsm}"` runs). It is quoted here as the limit on how precisely the absolute
level transfers to the commercial step. The effects are what the design space rests on.

The effects the platform expected are the effects the study found. Pool HCP rises with
protein load, rises as elution buffer pH falls, and the two interact. Step yield falls when
a high load is combined with a high linear velocity. Two significant findings were not
anticipated in @sec-prior. The curvature in elution buffer pH was not predicted, and the
effect of end of pool collect on pool HCP has the opposite sign to the expectation that a
later cut trades purity for yield. Both are explained mechanistically in @sec-results, and
neither changes a classification or a range.

Three limitations bound the conclusions. The design space is not confirmed at scale at the
edges of its ranges, since the study was executed on a scale-down model and the commercial
step is run near its set-point. Resin cycle number was held constant, so the study says
nothing about performance late in the resin's validated life, and that remains under the
life-cycle controls of SOP-2008. The study used a single representative clarified harvest,
so it characterizes this step's parameters and not its sensitivity to a feed that differs
from the platform expectation (the harvest step that produces that feed is characterized in
PCR-004).

`{python} f"{n_dev}"` deviations were recorded, described in full in @sec-dev. One was an
elution buffer prepared below its target pH, which affected a single response-surface run.
The other was an out-of-trend leached Protein A result that was re-assayed. Both are
departures from the approved protocol, and neither changed a fitted effect, a classification
or the operating region. No parameter at this step needed the most stringent class of
control, and the two quality-linked parameters are both well controlled by measurement
before use.

# Conclusions

The Protein A capture step is characterized over the ranges in @tbl-params and its operating
region is defined. `{python} f"{n_params}"` parameters were assessed,
`{python} f"{n_mv}"` in a multivariate design and `{python} f"{n_uv}"` univariately, giving
`{python} f"{n_wccpp}"` well-controlled critical process parameters,
`{python} f"{n_kpp}"` key process parameters and `{python} f"{n_gpp}"` general process
parameters. The step has no critical process parameter.

Leached Protein A, the attribute this step sets, met its acceptance criterion of
`{python} f"{acc_lpa[0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{acc_lpa[1]:g}"` ppm in both designs, at a highest
measured value of `{python} f"{lpa_meas_hi:.2f}"` ppm, and the fitted model resolves no
effect of any studied parameter on it. The design space caps elution buffer pH at
`{python} f"{par_lpa_ph_nor[1]:.3g}"`, because above that point the upper bound of the 95 %
predictive interval for this attribute reaches the criterion (@sec-par). Pool host
cell protein is governed by elution buffer pH and protein load through a response surface
that predicts a held-out run with a predicted R² of
`{python} f"{fit_r[HCP]['predR2']:.3f}"`. At the drug substance (@tbl-cap), the tightest of the three
attributes this step governs is host cell protein, at Cpk =
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp','Cpk']:.2f}"` with a mean of
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp','mean']:.1f}"` ng/mg against a limit of
`{python} f"{CAPR.loc['hcp','acc_high']:g}"` ng/mg.

`{python} f"{n_dev}"` deviations were investigated and dispositioned as retained, with no
effect on the classifications or on the region defined in @sec-ds. Every conclusion above is
bounded by the characterization ranges, by the fitted models and by the qualified scale-down
model they were fitted on, and none of them is confirmed at commercial scale until Stage 2.
The step does not by itself assure the drug substance limit for host cell protein and makes
no viral clearance claim. These results roll up into PCMR-001.

# Deviations from the plan {#sec-dev}

`{python} f"{n_dev}"` deviations from PCP-005 were recorded during execution. Each was
investigated, assigned a root cause, impact-assessed against the study conclusions and
dispositioned. Both were dispositioned as retained, which means the affected data were kept
in the reported analysis. @tbl-dev is the register.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print("\n: Deviations recorded during execution of PCP-005. {#tbl-dev}")
```

The two entries differ in kind. The first is a preparation error that put a studied
parameter away from its target on one run (response-surface run
`{python} f"{dev1_run}"`). The second is an analytical result that was rejected on review
and repeated. Neither invalidated a design, so no part of this study was re-executed.

## DEV-005-01 — elution buffer prepared below target pH

The elution buffer used on response-surface run `{python} f"{dev1_run}"` was released at pH
`{python} f"{dev_005_01_ph_measured:g}"` against a target of
`{python} f"{P.param('elution_ph').setpoint:g}"`, a departure of
`{python} f"{dev1_drop:.2f}"` pH units. The deviation was detected during
`{python} DEVS.loc['DEV-005-01','detected_during']`. Elution buffer pH carries the largest
effect on pool HCP of any parameter studied (@tbl-appc1), so a departure of this size is
material and is assessed on that basis and not dismissed as small.

The investigation traced the cause to a titration endpoint error during preparation of lot
`{python} dev1_lot` (`{python} dev1_vendor`), which is the buffer lot the deviation record
names. The pH was read before the buffer had equilibrated, and the correction added on that
reading overshot. No other lot from the same preparation session was used in the study, and
the release procedure in SOP-2103 was reinforced with an equilibration hold before the
endpoint reading.

The impact assessment turned on three things. The measured pH of
`{python} f"{dev_005_01_ph_measured:g}"` lies inside the characterization range for elution
buffer pH, at a coded position of `{python} f"{dev1_coded:.2f}"`, so the affected run
remains inside the region the response-surface model covers. Run
`{python} f"{dev1_run}"` is an axial run for end of pool collect, so its design setting for
elution buffer pH was the set-point, and at the recorded pH the fitted model predicts
`{python} f"{hcp_at_measured:,.0f}"` ng/mg of pool HCP against
`{python} f"{hcp_at_target:,.0f}"` ng/mg at target. The measured result for that run was
`{python} f"{run_obs:,.0f}"` ng/mg, which is close to the prediction at target and gives a
standardized residual of `{python} f"{run_resid:.2f}"` against the fitted model. The run's
influence on the fit is correspondingly small: its Cook's distance is
`{python} f"{run_cook:.3f}"`, against a maximum of `{python} f"{cook_max:.3f}"` across the
`{python} f"{n_rsm}"` runs of the design.

The run was therefore retained with its design setting. The recorded response is consistent
with that setting and not with the offset the buffer record implies, and the leverage the
run has on the fit is small, so keeping it does not materially change the fitted surface.
The deviation is nonetheless the reason the control strategy in @sec-control keeps buffer pH
release testing as a named control.

## DEV-005-02 — leached Protein A result out of trend on first assay

A leached Protein A result was flagged as out of trend during
`{python} DEVS.loc['DEV-005-02','detected_during']`, before the data set was released for
analysis, because the initial value was inconsistent with the other results from the same
assay plate and with the rest of the leached Protein A results in the study.

The investigation suspected carryover on the ELISA plate. The retained sample was re-assayed
under `{python} dev2_method` on a fresh plate with additional wash steps, and the repeat
gave `{python} f"{dev_005_02_retest_ppm:g}"` ppm (above the method's limit of quantitation
of `{python} MPERF.loc['AMV-3016','LOQ']`). The initial result was rejected under the
method's own repeat criteria and the repeat was accepted in its place. The register does not
link the deviation to a numbered run, so the affected sample is not identified in the design
matrices of Appendix A and Appendix B.

The impact on the study is bounded by two figures. The retest value of
`{python} f"{dev_005_02_retest_ppm:g}"` ppm is well inside the acceptance criterion of
`{python} f"{acc_lpa[0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{acc_lpa[1]:g}"` ppm, and it sits inside the
spread the centre points show for this response, which is
`{python} f"{cv_r.loc[LBL[LPA],'%CV']:.1f}"` % at the set-point. Since no factor effect on
leached Protein A was resolved by either design (@sec-rsm), no conclusion of this report
depends on the value of any single leached Protein A result. The deviation was dispositioned
as retained and no re-execution was required.

```{python}
print("\n: Screening effects on leached Protein A. No term is significant. {#tbl-appc3}")
```

@tbl-appc7.
